chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said, 'May Allah improve you. We mix with a group of the people of As-Sawad (Iraq), so we lend them money, and they send us the produce/crops from their lands, so we sell it to them for a profit, and we have benefit in that.' He said, 'There is no harm.' And I do not know him except to have said, 'If it were not for what they send us from their produce, we would not lend them.' He said, 'There is no harm.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ السَّوَادِ: People of As-Sawad (a region in Iraq known for agriculture)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to lend money to someone and then buy their crops from them at a higher price?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates a common commercial practice where lenders purchase agricultural produce from borrowers, effectively embedding interest-like benefits within the trade price. The Imam’s affirmation highlights the flexibility of *fiqh al-mu'amalat* in recognizing that the primary motive for lending—securing goods at a favorable rate—does not invalidate the transaction, provided the exchange itself is valid. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that such arrangements are permissible as long as they do not constitute explicit riba in the loan contract itself.
